images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of the IIMT framework and editor paradigms. (a) The pipeline: OCR extracts text → a translator produces the translation → a scene text editor generates the output image. (b) Rule-based: remove, render, and paste separately. (c) Training-based: a learned GAN or diffusion editor (requires extra training). (d) FlowTranslator (ours): training-free flow editing with trajectory controls (CE and RCR) for text translation with background preservation.

Figure 2:Overview of FlowTranslator. OCR extracts the source text and forms a source caption, while a frozen LLM translates it to obtain the target caption. A frozen VAE encodes the source image intoZ0srcZ^{\mathrm{src}}_{0}, from which noise initialization producesZTFEZ^{\mathrm{FE}}_{T}. At each editing step, the same frozen DiT predicts source- and target-conditioned velocities. Their difference updates the flow-editing latent. RCR perturbs the target-branch noise within the detected text region, and CE amplifies the accumulated displacement before it is fed back to the target branch. The final latentZ0FEZ^{\mathrm{FE}}_{0}is decoded to produce the translated image.

Figure 3:Qualitative results on TTV. Each row shows the source image, the benchmark target image, and the FlowTranslator output for one translation direction. The examples cover EN→\rightarrowDE, FR→\rightarrowEN, DE→\rightarrowEN, and RO→\rightarrowEN.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison on whole-image ScenePair En→Zh translation. For each example, we show the source image (with red boxes marking text to be translated), the requested target text, and outputs of existing open-source methods, followed by FlowTranslator. FlowTranslator renders the requested Chinese text within the original region. It preserves both the surrounding scene and the local text appearance.

Figure S3:Additional qualitative examples of full-image scene text translation
into Chinese. Each pair shows the source image on the left and the corresponding
FlowTranslator output on the right.
